verdict.rationale: The only evidence is that Solo firmware builds with a default attestation key, and that users can generate, sign and program their own attestation key pair, even across many devices. That implies the key emits attestation a relying party could check. However, these docs come from the customization and building pages, which reference the STM32L432 (Solo 1) build, so applicability to Solo 2 is unclear. Nothing documents how a relying party verifies genuineness or enforces approved models at registration. Missing for 10: Solo 2-specific attestation certificate chain/root CA publication, AAGUID or FIDO Metadata Service listing for model allowlisting, documented registration-time verification flow, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, I can verify device attestation at registration to enforce that only genuine, approved key models are enrolled

citations.quote: If you don't want to use the default attestation key that Solo builds with, you can create your own and program it.
Now to generate & sign the attestation key pair that will go on your device, or maybe 100,000 devices :)
